summary: Apremilast is an oral small-molecule phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) inhibitor that raises intracellular cAMP and modulates inflammatory cytokine production. It treats active psoriatic arthritis, plaque psoriasis (candidates for phototherapy/systemic therapy) and oral ulcers of Behcet disease. It requires an initial dose titration to limit gastrointestinal side effects, needs no routine laboratory monitoring, and carries warnings for diarrhea/nausea/vomiting, depression and weight loss.
indications: Active psoriatic arthritis in adults and children >=6 years weighing >=20 kg
Plaque psoriasis in adults who are candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy; moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in children >=6 years (>=20 kg)
Oral ulcers associated with Behcet's disease in adults

dosage.d: Day1 10 mg AM; Day2 10 mg AM + 10 mg PM; Day3 10 mg AM + 20 mg PM; Day4 20 mg AM + 20 mg PM; Day5 20 mg AM + 30 mg PM
30 mg twice daily (or OTEZLA XR 75 mg once daily)
20 mg twice daily after weight-based titration
30 mg once daily; during titration use only the AM schedule and skip PM doses

admin: Follow the 5-day titration schedule to minimize diarrhea, nausea and vomiting
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush, split or chew (especially XR)
May be taken with or without food (XR also without regard to meals)
In severe renal impairment use only the morning titration doses and a 30 mg once-daily maintenance dose
Re-titrate if therapy is interrupted for a prolonged period
moa: Apremilast is a small-molecule inhibitor of phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) specific for cyclic AMP. PDE4 inhibition raises intracellular cAMP, which down-regulates the inflammatory response by decreasing production of pro-inflammatory cytokines (such as TNF-alpha, IL-23, IL-17) and increasing anti-inflammatory mediators. The precise mechanism by which this produces clinical benefit is not fully defined.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to apremilast or any excipient in the formulation
relative: History of depression or suicidal thoughts/behavior
Significant unexplained or ongoing weight loss
monitor: Patients with persistent severe GI symptoms
Elderly or dehydrated patients (volume depletion from diarrhea/vomiting)

preg: Available human data have not identified a clear drug-associated risk of major birth defects, but animal studies showed dose-related abortion/embryo-fetal loss; apremilast may increase the risk of fetal loss. Advise pregnant women of the potential risk and use only if clearly needed. A pregnancy exposure registry exists.
lact: There are no data on the presence of apremilast in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding alongside the mother's clinical need and any potential adverse effect on the infant.
renal: In severe renal impairment (CrCl below 30 mL/min) apremilast exposure is increased; reduce the maintenance dose to 30 mg once daily and during titration use only the morning schedule, skipping afternoon doses. No adjustment is needed for mild-to-moderate impairment.
hepatic: Pharmacokinetics are not significantly altered in hepatic impairment; no dosage adjustment is required for mild, moderate or severe hepatic impairment.

major: Strong CYP450 inducers (rifampin, phenobarbital, carbamazepine, phenytoin) - decrease apremilast exposure and may cause loss of efficacy; concomitant use not recommended
interactions.food: No clinically meaningful effect of food on absorption; may be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: No specific pharmacokinetic interaction; alcohol may aggravate gastrointestinal upset or depressive symptoms.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; routine lab monitoring is not required.

serious: Severe diarrhea, nausea or vomiting with dehydration
Depression, suicidal thoughts or mood changes
emergency: Severe dehydration from refractory GI symptoms

monitoring: Body weight at baseline and regularly; evaluate and consider discontinuation for significant unexplained weight loss
Mood and behavior - watch for new or worsening depression or suicidal thoughts
Gastrointestinal tolerance; consider dose reduction or suspension for severe diarrhea, nausea or vomiting
Hydration status, particularly in elderly patients
counsel: Follow the starter-pack titration schedule exactly to reduce stomach upset
Tell your doctor about new or worsening depression, mood changes or thoughts of self-harm
Report severe or persistent diarrhea, nausea or vomiting and any significant weight loss
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or chew
Do not start without telling your doctor about other medicines, especially seizure drugs or rifampin
pk: Clinical improvement typically over several weeks of therapy
Twice-daily (or once-daily XR) dosing maintains effect
OTEZLA below 30 C; OTEZLA XR 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C)
pearls: The 5-day dose titration is essential to limit diarrhea, nausea and vomiting, which are most common in the first weeks
Apremilast needs no routine laboratory monitoring, unlike methotrexate or biologics, making it convenient for patients who cannot have frequent blood tests
Counsel about depression and weight loss - monitor mood and weight at every visit
Strong CYP450 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital) markedly reduce efficacy and should be avoided
In severe renal impairment, halve the dosing frequency to 30 mg once daily and use AM-only titration
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and resume the usual schedule. Do not take two doses at once. If you have stopped for several days, ask your prescriber whether you need to re-titrate.
overdose: There is no specific information on overdose treatment or a specific antidote. In the event of overdose, discontinue apremilast and provide general supportive care with monitoring for exaggerated effects such as gastrointestinal symptoms. Manage symptomatically.
